title: Not only Scripture-contrary traditions — Christ damns human precepts as such
source_text: XXX. Ad illud vero quod dicunt adversarii Judaeorum traditiones fuisse sacrae Scripturae contrarias, suas vero non item: observandum est multas Judaeorum traditiones non fuisse directe, & sua natura legi divinae contrarias, sed tantum quatenus erant legis additamenta, cum lex divina quicquam sibi addi prohibeat. Ita mos ille abluendi manus religione quadam ante cibi sumptionem ex se nihil mali habere videtur, nec quod sit directe Scripturae contrarium. Et tamen haec est illa ipsa traditio quam speciatim carpit Christus. Quod si dicant Pontificii saltem inanem esse, verum quidem illi dicent. At non minus quadrat in illorum traditiones. Nec enim minus inanes & vanae sunt. Quod si res ex humanae rationis judicio aestimetur, mos ille Judaeorum comperietur non minorem sapientiae speciem habere, quam Pontificiorum pleraque instituta. Sed Christus non damnat simpliciter Judaeorum traditiones, vel quia inanes erant, vel quia erant Scripturae contrariae; sed praeterea in genere, quoniam erant mandata & doctrinae hominum. Quod de traditionibus Pontificiorum non minus verum est.
pass_a_gloss: But to that which the adversaries say — that the Jews' traditions were contrary to sacred Scripture, but theirs are not — it must be observed that many Jewish traditions were not directly and by their own nature contrary to the divine law, but only insofar as they were additions to the law, since the divine law forbids anything to be added to itself. Thus that custom of washing the hands with a certain religious care before taking food seems to have nothing evil in itself, nor anything directly contrary to Scripture. And yet this is the very tradition which Christ specially attacks. But if the Pontiffs say it is at least empty, they will indeed say what is true. Yet that fits their traditions no less. For they are no less empty and vain. And if the matter is judged by human reason, that Jewish custom will be found to have no lesser appearance of wisdom than most of the Pontiffs' institutes. But Christ does not simply condemn the Jews' traditions either because they were empty or because they were contrary to Scripture; but further, in general, because they were commandments and doctrines of men. Which is no less true of the Pontiffs' traditions.
pass_b_english: Rome says Jewish traditions contradicted Scripture, but theirs do not.
Many Jewish traditions were not evil or directly anti-Scripture by nature — only unlawful as additions, since divine law forbids adding to itself.
Hand-washing before meals looks harmless and not directly against Scripture — yet that is the very tradition Christ specially targets.
Calling it empty helps Rome nothing: their traditions are no less empty, and by mere human wisdom Jewish washings look no less wise than most Roman institutes.
Christ's verdict is broader: He damns them not only as empty or contrary, but in general as human commandments and doctrines — and that charge fits Rome's traditions equally.

lemmas.gloss: forbids anything to be added to itself
in general ... commandments and doctrines of men

choices.why: Deut-style no-add rule, not only direct contradiction.
